title: TBD, A First-person survival in an overgrown far-future city
author: Forsaken_Support3671
selftext:
I’m making **THE BLACKOUT DISTRICT (TBD)**, a single-player first-person survival game set in an overgrown, dead far-future city, inspired by the Roblox game *Blackout: Revival*. I’m not a programmer: I make the design calls and test everything, and Claude Code (in the Claude desktop app) writes the code in Godot 4 / GDScript.

**What’s in the video / what works so far:**

* **Movement & climbing:** vaulting, ledge grabs, shimmying, ledge walking with a balance system, free climbing and pipes. Your arms, legs and breath get tired, and it shows in how you move.
* **No health bar:** blood is your health. Wounds land on specific body parts and bleed, and a shot leg makes you limp. A shot arm makes your aim shake and can tear you off a ledge. Lose too much blood and the screen greys out until you pass out.
* **Guns:** pistol, rifle and pump shotgun, with aim-down-sights through the real iron sights. Bullets go where the barrel points, not to the middle of the screen, so a shaky arm really misses. Magazines drop, the slide locks back on the last round, and shotgun shells load one at a time.
* **Enemy soldiers:** they see you in a cone, hear your shots and call you out to each other. They fire aimed bursts, find cover, pop up to shoot, and bleed out like you do.
* **Blocky R10 characters** (R6 proportions with elbows and knees), wearing Roblox classic clothing templates.

**How the AI side works:**

* I describe what I want in plain language and Claude plans it, writes it, then runs automated tests and renders screenshots off-screen to check its own work before showing me. There are 8 test suites now (climbing, health, guns, hits, NPCs...).
* I steer the feel (“the hands tweak when I turn fast”, “the dropped mag floats”, “ADS should zoom more”) and it tracks down the cause and fixes it.
* Assets are mine or downloaded: gun models from free sources, gun sounds from my own collection. Claude wires them in, splits the models into moving parts (slides, pumps, magazines), and fixes broken files.
* It’s all running on an AMD HD 8570, a very weak GPU, so performance is a constant consideration.

**Next up:** a proper combat test map, then inventory, healing items and the actual city.

Happy to answer questions about the workflow, or about what worked and what didn’t.
